variables.reason: The ledger variable Ra is defined as the first-order absolute moment of height fluctuations (arithmetic mean roughness). The KB entry pq_arithmetic_mean_roughness explicitly lists symbols Ra / R_a, gives the same definition (mean absolute deviation of surface height) and records si_dimension = L (length). pq_mean_roughness_height provides an equivalent canonical mean roughness-height entry and also has si_dimension = L. Both records therefore directly apply to the ledger Ra variable (matching symbol, definition and domain) and together support the full SI vector with L exponent = 1 and all other base exponents = 0.

The ledger variable kt is described as the peak-to-valley height. The KB entry pq_peak_to_valley_height uses symbols including kt and defines this quantity as a vertical height difference between peaks and valleys; it explicitly lists si_dimension = L. pq_mean_roughness_height is an additional length-valued roughness-height record. Both entries directly apply to the ledger kt variable (matching symbol/alias and physical description) and support the SI exponents with L = 1 and zeros elsewhere.

The ledger variable k_rms is the root-mean-square height of surface roughness. KB entry pq_rms_roughness_height defines the root-mean-square fluctuation of surface height about its mean and lists si_dimension = L. pq_mean_roughness_height provides an equivalent length-valued roughness-height canonical entry. These KB records match the ledger variable by symbol and definition and fully support the SI vector L=1, all others 0.

The ledger variable Sk is the skewness of roughness height fluctuations. KB entry pq_height_skewness defines surface-height skewness as the third standardized moment, lists symbols Sk / S_k and explicitly records si_dimension = 1 (dimensionless standardized moment). The record directly applies by symbol and definition and therefore supports the ledger's all-zero SI exponent vector (dimensionless).

The ledger variable Ku is the kurtosis of roughness height fluctuations. KB entry pq_height_kurtosis defines surface-height kurtosis as the fourth standardized moment, lists symbols Ku / K_u and explicitly records si_dimension = 1 (dimensionless). This entry matches the ledger variable by definition and symbol and supports the dimensionless SI vector (all zeros).

The ledger variable ES is the effective streamwise slope of the roughness. KB entry pq_effective_surface_slope defines mean absolute surface slope or streamwise effective slope, and notes that a surface-height derivative is length divided by length and therefore dimensionless; si_dimension = 1. The symbol ES is used in the KB entry and the definition corresponds to the ledger variable, supporting the all-zero SI exponent vector (dimensionless).

The ledger variable Po is surface porosity. KB entry pq_porosity lists symbols Po / P_o and defines porosity as a fraction of void area/volume; it explicitly records si_dimension = 1 (dimensionless fraction). The KB record directly matches the ledger variable by symbol and physical definition and fully supports the all-zero SI exponent vector (dimensionless).

variables.reason: The ledger variable Ra is defined as the first-order absolute moment of height fluctuations (arithmetic mean roughness). The KB entry pq_arithmetic_mean_roughness explicitly lists symbols Ra / R_a, gives the same definition (mean absolute deviation of surface height) and records si_dimension = L (length). pq_mean_roughness_height provides an equivalent canonical mean roughness-height entry and also has si_dimension = L. Both records therefore directly apply to the ledger Ra variable (matching symbol, definition and domain) and together support the full SI vector with L exponent = 1 and all other base exponents = 0.

The ledger variable kt is described as the peak-to-valley height. The KB entry pq_peak_to_valley_height uses symbols including kt and defines this quantity as a vertical height difference between peaks and valleys; it explicitly lists si_dimension = L. pq_mean_roughness_height is an additional length-valued roughness-height record. Both entries directly apply to the ledger kt variable (matching symbol/alias and physical description) and support the SI exponents with L = 1 and zeros elsewhere.

The ledger variable k_rms is the root-mean-square height of surface roughness. KB entry pq_rms_roughness_height defines the root-mean-square fluctuation of surface height about its mean and lists si_dimension = L. pq_mean_roughness_height provides an equivalent length-valued roughness-height canonical entry. These KB records match the ledger variable by symbol and definition and fully support the SI vector L=1, all others 0.

The ledger variable Sk is the skewness of roughness height fluctuations. KB entry pq_height_skewness defines surface-height skewness as the third standardized moment, lists symbols Sk / S_k and explicitly records si_dimension = 1 (dimensionless standardized moment). The record directly applies by symbol and definition and therefore supports the ledger's all-zero SI exponent vector (dimensionless).

The ledger variable Ku is the kurtosis of roughness height fluctuations. KB entry pq_height_kurtosis defines surface-height kurtosis as the fourth standardized moment, lists symbols Ku / K_u and explicitly records si_dimension = 1 (dimensionless). This entry matches the ledger variable by definition and symbol and supports the dimensionless SI vector (all zeros).

The ledger variable ES is the effective streamwise slope of the roughness. KB entry pq_effective_surface_slope defines mean absolute surface slope or streamwise effective slope, and notes that a surface-height derivative is length divided by length and therefore dimensionless; si_dimension = 1. The symbol ES is used in the KB entry and the definition corresponds to the ledger variable, supporting the all-zero SI exponent vector (dimensionless).

The ledger variable Po is surface porosity. KB entry pq_porosity lists symbols Po / P_o and defines porosity as a fraction of void area/volume; it explicitly records si_dimension = 1 (dimensionless fraction). The KB record directly matches the ledger variable by symbol and physical definition and fully supports the all-zero SI exponent vector (dimensionless).
